hits.dead_ends:
DTAM/DT-AM circular sweeps, all negative:
1. Server-side CDX filters on matchType=domain return HTTP 200 with an EMPTY body when matches are sparse — a silent timeout, not "no matches". I proved the filter mechanism works (filter=original:.*pdf.* returns rows immediately) and then stopped trusting sparse-pattern filters, sweeping locally instead. Anyone repeating this work should not read an empty filtered CDX response as a negative.
2. CDX &page= pagination is unreliable for this domain: url=sgx.com/wps/wcm/connect* reports showNumPages=2, page 0 returns 1,404 rows truncated mid-alphabet at GUID 68f6138..., and page 1 returns 0 rows. Use &limit=N&showResumeKey=true and follow the resume key instead. (Also: BSD head has no `head -n -2`; that silently discarded a whole sweep before I caught it.)
3. Complete resume-key sweep of matchType=host sgx.com (38,689 unique URLs, covering sgx.com, www.sgx.com and www2.sgx.com — the IA canonicaliser strips www\d* so all three share one urlkey): exactly one DTAM URL, the 2006 DTAM56OF2006APPENDIX2.pdf. Zero 2019 circulars.
4. Complete sweep of api2.sgx.com (5,241 unique URLs): DTAM PDFs from 2022/2023/2024/2025 only. Nothing from 2019-2020.
5. The known-good example from my brief, /wps/wcm/connect/2edf7596-b337-4d2d-ab19-eabf72240661/DTAM+84+of+2018+-+Trading+Schedules+for+Year+End+2018_New+Year+Day+2019.pdf, has ZERO CDX rows under any prefix I tried. That class of URL was never crawled.
6. CDX prefix sweeps of sgx.com/regulation/circulars*, sgx.com/securities/circulars*, sgx.com/derivatives/circulars* — all return zero rows. Those paths were never archived because they do not exist: SGX's live sitemap.xml (1,222 URLs, "Last Update 15 Sep 2022") contains no member-circulars index page at all. DT/AM circulars are not published in a public listing on sgx.com.
7. api.sgx.com (880 archived URLs) exposes https://api.sgx.com/circulars/v1.0 — but that is the ISSUER prospectus/shareholder-circular API (parameters companyname, prospectustype, documentdatestart), not member circulars.
8. Subdomains with ZERO captures in the archive: member.sgx.com, memberlink.sgx.com, dt.sgx.com, titan.sgx.com, static.sgx.com, infofeed.sgx.com, apiv2.sgx.com, sgxgroup.com.
9. All four T+1 newsletters, plus the two 2018 trading-hours newsletters, download fine (HTTP 200, correct byte counts) and are then unreadable: /Filter /Standard, /V 4, /R 4, /Length 128, /P -1028, /EncryptMetadata true. Poppler and pikepdf both reject the empty password. With EncryptMetadata true even /Info and XMP are ciphertext, so not one byte of title, date or body is recoverable. I did not attempt to guess or crack passwords.
10. The retired portal page derivatives_trading_hours_and_calendar/Trading+Hours has only 7 captures ever, and NONE between 2018-07-11 and 2021-09-25 — a 38-month hole straddling the entire change window.
11. The new-site page sgx.com/derivatives/trading has 47 captures, earliest 2020-08-03. No 2019 capture exists.
12. No SGX media release about the T+1 extension is archived: grepping every archived media-centre URL for hour/trading/extension/T+1 returns only unrelated 2019-2020 items.
13. rulebook.sgx.com "2019" rule-amendment index lists one "Amendments to the Futures Trading Rules" entry and nothing about trading hours — SGX sets derivatives session times by circular and contract spec, not by rulebook amendment, so that route cannot date the change.
14. Four WebSearch queries for the circular text ("Extension of T+1 Trading Hours" + DT/AM, "Circular No. DT/AM" + T+1, etc.) surfaced nothing; the only relevant broker republication found (Phillip Nova) concerns a different change, "the trading hours will be extended from Monday, 4 November 2024".
15. Guessed filename probes against the live api2 file store (5 title variants x 6 folders 2019-07..2019-12, e.g. Extension%20of%20T%2B1%20Trading%20Hours.pdf) all returned 404.

THE ONE LIVE LEAD WORTH A FOLLOW-UP PASS: SGX still serves 2019 DT/AM circulars that the Wayback Machine never crawled. I proved this by retrieving Circular No. DT/AM - 86 of 2019 (19 Dec 2019) directly from https://api2.sgx.com/sites/default/files/2019-12/... — it has no CDX record at all. So the T+1 extension circular may well be sitting live in a files/2019-07 .. files/2019-11 folder under a descriptive filename. What is missing is an index: api2 exposes no directory listing, and I could not locate SGX's search API (the sgx.com JS shell chunk I fetched contains no api endpoints; the real search bundle is in a chunk I did not chase). Finding SGX's site-search or media-entity API (URLs of the form ...pdf?destination=/media/163261 hint at Drupal media IDs) is the highest-value next step for this channel.

(b) More insidiously, a regex filter containing square brackets, e.g. filter=original:.*[Cc]alendar.*, makes curl treat "[Cc]" as a glob range and abort with exit 3 "URL malformed" BEFORE any request — printing nothing at all, which looks exactly like an empty archive result.
